findings.text: - **Treating dividend policy as a residual decision.** Buffett's view that paying dividends is "almost a last resort for corporate management" [BT] reflects a preference for reinvesting excess funds (Ch 11.2); the payout is a capital-allocation choice to explain, not a residual.
findings.problem: With the signalling claim removed, the only evidence left under this anti-pattern cuts against its heading. Buffett's 'last resort' view (pay dividends only once reinvestment options are used up) is the residual approach to dividends, so the bullet cites a view that endorses the thing it names as an anti-pattern. The attributed content is supported; the repaired bullet no longer argues coherently.
findings.evidence: Deep 415: Buffett holds that companies are usually better off reinvesting excess funds in infrastructure, evolving technologies, and other profitable ventures [BT] (Ch 11.2). Source 18532-18536.
findings.fix: correct: - **Paying out cash without weighing reinvestment.** Buffett's view that paying dividends is "almost a last resort for corporate management" [BT] reflects a preference for reinvesting excess funds in infrastructure, evolving technologies, and other profitable ventures (Ch 11.2); explain any payout against the reinvestment it forgoes. | strip
